title: Senior Software Engineer II - Enterprise Foundations
description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart , we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work-whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop-while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Overview
Enterprise Foundations is the engineering team responsible for the architectural and integration work that allows Instacart 's Retailer Platform to scale across the world's largest grocers. Our work spans omnichannel integrations - bringing products like FoodStorm catering and Caper Carts onto unified Instacart platform rails - enterprise extensibility (sandbox environments, configuration systems, retailer-facing tooling), and the cross-cutting data isolation work that allows Instacart 's ML and Data Engineering teams to safely build bespoke models on top of the platform. As Instacart 's enterprise retail business expands to hundreds of partner brands and new international markets, this team's work is foundational to how the platform matures.
We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer II to own and ship one of the team's most complex multi-quarter work-streams - at the seam of omnichannel identity, international storefront search expansions, and partner-owned integrations that we ultimately operate ourselves. You'll be the technical DRI for your area: framing the problem, designing the systems, driving the rollout, and codifying the patterns so the rest of Enterprise Platform can adopt them without your direct involvement. You'll work closely with Staff engineers on the team who set the team-wide architectural thesis, and partner across Connected Stores, Professional Services, Commerce, Search, Data Engineering, and ML to land integrations that hold up across organizational boundaries.
About the Job

• Own a multi-quarter integration workstream end to end - for example, unified customer identity across FoodStorm and Storefront Pro, international storefront and search expansion for enterprise retailers, or consolidation of bespoke retailer-vertical services onto shared Instacart platform rails - from problem framing through design, implementation, rollout, and deprecation of legacy paths.

• Lead vendor and cross-team integrations where Instacart will eventually own the system - push for the right observability, fallback behavior, and cost/latency guardrails up front, and challenge partner designs early rather than inheriting them at handoff.

• Build reusable patterns, frameworks, and templates that other engineers across Enterprise Foundations and adjacent teams adopt with minimal hand-holding; treat "system at a glance" docs and migration runbooks as first-class deliverables.

• Operate hands-on as a senior individual contributor on the highest-leverage technical work in your area; raise the bar on design quality, code quality, observability, and operational rigor.

• Manage cash balances and prepare the weekly cash forecast

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance and 3-5 years of progressive general ledger accounting experience; CPA or CPA-track preferred.

description:

Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement - built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before.

The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Zip’s team includes product leaders from Apple, Airbnb, and Meta, as well as former procurement leaders from United Health, Sanofi, MGM Resorts, Discover, and NASA.

Backed by Adams Street, Alkeon, BOND, CRV, DST, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator, Zip has raised $371 million, most recently at a $2.2 billion valuation and has been recognized by Forbes Fintech 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, Inc. Best in Business, and LinkedIn Top Startups.

YOUR ROLE

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager (TPM) to own Zip's engineering brand: the programs that make our engineering team visible, credible and worth joining for the engineers we want to hire and keep. This includes running the engineering blog and its publishing rhythm, building the public voices of our engineers through talks and bylines, and organizing the meetups, mixers and events where engineers meet our team.

You'll work directly with engineers to find the stories in the work they do, coach them into writing and speaking about it, and turn those stories into content that candidates find before a recruiter reaches them.

You'll partner with Recruiting, Product Marketing, Product Operations, Data Science, and our growing Engineering org to build a public technical presence of Zip.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Run the engineering blog end to end: Source topics from teams, coach engineer authors, edit to a high bar, and move posts through legal, security and comms review without letting them stall. Hold a publishing rhythm the org can rely on, such as a pool of three drafts with one post out each week.

- Own distribution: Share posts where engineers read, including Hacker News, TLDR, Pragmatic Engineer and engineering newsletters, and decide what our social channels are for.

- Build engineer voices: Help engineers develop a public presence through bylines, talks and speaker preparation, including an employee ambassador program that lets them share their work in their own voices.

- Run our external presence: Sponsor meetups, organize mixers and hackathons, and set conference strategy: where we speak, where we sponsor and where we skip. Own the budget and vendors behind it.

- Pursue top-company recognition: Identify the lists and rankings that matter to engineers, such as LinkedIn Top Companies and fintech lists, and run the submissions and supporting content.

- Partner with Recruiting: Help build the funnel with candidate-facing content such as engineer spotlights, team stories and interview preparation material, and support the referral program.

- Run internal engineering programs: Produce engineering-wide meetings, engineer onboarding experience, engineering mobility program and other internal processes that support the growth of engineers.

- Measure what matters: With Data Science and Recruiting, track technical reach, content engagement, community growth, and the quality and source of inbound engineering candidates. Be straight about what can and cannot be attributed to hiring.

WHAT YOU BRING

- 3+ years in Technical Program Management, engineering communications, community management, technical or employer brand at a fast-paced technology company.

- Bachelor's and/or Master's degree, preferably in Computer Science or another technical field, or years of working directly with engineers.

- Technical fluency: you don't need to write production code, but you can follow a design doc, hold a systems design conversation, and know exactly how to shape what comes out of that conversation
